correctness.rationale: For x=r e^{iθ}, membership is r≤[cos(θ−2πj/n)]_+. Ordering angular vertex distances in half-sector 0≤θ≤π/n gives kth radial cutoff cos(a_k+s_k θ). For k≥2, the second cutoff never exceeds r_P=cosδ/cos(δ−θ), so the polar integral has no polygon clipping. I independently evaluated numerical rank-cutoff quadratures against the printed closed trigonometric tails for all k at n=3,4,5,6,11,20, agreeing within 1e−7; the angular and monotonicity proof extends to arbitrary integer n. Origin belongs to all n disks but has zero area.
